The test image shows a mango leaf with the following features:
- Elongated leaf with serrated margins
- Brown, dried, irregular damage concentrated along the leaf margins and tips of teeth
- No white powdery coating (not Powdery Mildew)
- No black sooty layer (not Sooty Mould)
- No galls or swellings (not Gall Midge)
- Green tissue otherwise intact, no large necrotic lesions spreading inward (less consistent with Die Back or Bacterial Canker)
- The damage pattern shows characteristic notching and scalloped cutouts along the entire leaf margin, consistent with weevil feeding

This pattern of irregular marginal notching/cutting with dried brown edges is the hallmark of Cutting Weevil damage on mango leaves.
